newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania's main opposition appeals to Berisha.
newsitem.headline: Albania's main opposition appeals to Berisha.

text.p: Albania's main opposition Socialist Party said it had appealed to President Sali Berisha at a meeting on Tuesday to agree to a new broad-based government to help end the violent unrest gripping the country.

But one of the Socialist leaders, Pandeli Majko, said the party had gained "no sense of compromise" from Berisha at the talks, the first since parliament declared a national state of emergency to crack down on armed chaos in southern Albania.
"His (Berisha's) response was 'you must not try to take power by arms'," Majko told Reuters. "We advised him that we would never want power through blood," he said.
Officials in Berisha's ruling Democratic Party, whose leader Tritan Shehu was also at the talks according to Majko, were not immediately available for comment on the meeting.

The Democrat-controlled parliament declared a state of emergency on Sunday after an announcement by Berisha that his unpopular Prime Minister Aleksander Meksi would resign failed to calm the southern disturbances.

Majko said he did not believe state of emergency measures could calm the situation. "It is no longer a matter of left or right but of protecting people and stopping further blood from being shed," he said of the call for a broad government.
